I have farmed this land all my life, just like my father and his father before him. We are in Quzhou, in the flat plain of Hebei. Everyone here grows wheat and corn — one after the other, same ground, all year. That is what the land is for. That is what the buyers want. I do not think about growing something different. What would I do with it? Who would buy it?

My land is about 8 mu. In autumn I put wheat in. After I cut the wheat in June, I plant corn on the same ground. The corn comes out in September. Then wheat again. This is the cycle. I have done it every year.

I plough before the wheat because my father ploughed. It loosens the soil and kills the weeds. For the corn I use the rotary machine — it is faster, and the ground is still soft from the wheat season.

I buy the wheat seed from the village seed shop, the kind everyone uses. For corn I buy hybrid — the seeds with the special bags. Everyone switched to hybrid corn years ago because the yield is better. Even I know that.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then add urea when the plants are growing. I do not measure exactly — I go by what I used last year and what my neighbor uses. I irrigate the wheat four times: before winter, in spring when it starts growing fast, when it heads, and once more when the grain is filling. Corn I irrigate once unless the summer rains are enough.

I spray for insects twice on the wheat — once in spring for aphids — and once on the corn for the borer worm.
